context: life-safety led · integrated smoke-control test + base-build/tenant fit-out interface govern the programme

brief.intro: New to this project type? A shopping mall or retail centre is a large, open public building wrapped around a network of leasable tenant units, built by the developer as a "base-build" shell that individual tenants then fit out separately. The programme is driven less by the structure itself than by two things: the integrated life-safety system — smoke control, fire, public-address voice evacuation and lift-homing all have to work together as one proven system before the mall can open — and the recurring handover boundary between base-build and tenant fit-out, repeated for every unit and food-court outlet. Long structural spans and atria also mean the steel frame and central mechanical plant are on the critical path early, well before finishes begin.

scope.desc: Earthworks, piling/foundations and basement or service-yard construction.

scope.desc: Long-span steel frame, floor slabs and atrium structure that create the mall's open volumes.

scope.desc: Cladding, roofing, glazing and waterproofing to get the shell weather-tight.

scope.name: Mechanical — central plant & HVAC
scope.desc: Chillers, AHUs and chilled-water distribution serving the mall's common areas.

scope.name: Electrical power & lighting
scope.desc: MV/LV distribution, standby generation and lighting for common areas, mall and car park.

scope.name: Fire protection & life safety
scope.desc: Sprinklers, smoke control/extraction and the fire alarm & voice-evacuation system.

scope.name: Vertical transport
scope.desc: Escalators, travelators and lifts serving mall levels and atria.

scope.name: ELV / security & BMS
scope.desc: CCTV, access control, the PA system and the building management system that ties everything together.

scope.name: Mall common-area finishes
scope.desc: Flooring/stone, ceilings, signage and wayfinding in the public areas.

scope.name: Tenant fit-out interface & handover
scope.desc: Base-build handover packages issued per unit and coordination with tenants, anchors and food-court operators.

must_get_right: The integrated life-safety cause-and-effect test (smoke control + fire + voice evacuation + lift homing) is the real finish line, not the last fire-alarm point — protect real time for it and for re-tests.
Base-build must be substantially finished and formally handed over before tenant fit-out can start in each unit — track this as a milestone per unit, not an assumption.
Vertical transport has long procurement lead times and needs early shaft/pit readiness — sequence the structure around it, not the other way round.
Anchor tenants and food-court units often carry bespoke structural/MEP interfaces — coordinate these early; they are not "just another shop".

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Car-park, mall common areas and each tenant unit are tracked as separate zones so base-build and fit-out progress can be reported independently.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Structural steel and envelope run a 6-day week; MEP fit-out and finishes move to extended hours ahead of the life-safety test; tenant fit-out runs on its own calendar in parallel once base-build handover packages are issued per unit or zone.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs structural steel/envelope (weather-tight) → central-plant & vertical-transport installation → fire/life-safety device wiring → integrated smoke-control & voice-evacuation cause-and-effect test → base-build sign-off → phased tenant handover. The integrated life-safety test, not the last finish, is the true schedule gate to opening.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Design is frozen, the tenant lease/fit-out guide is finalised, anchor-tenant interfaces are agreed early, and authority approvals are obtained per phase gate. A single mobilisation is assumed.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Sites are often congested and urban; crane and heavy-lift windows are needed for steel and plant. Phased handover to multiple tenants competes for access late in the programme, and skilled commissioning resources are shared across systems near the life-safety test.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: anchor-tenant design changes, integrated life-safety re-test loops, and tenant fit-out coordination delays. Schedule contingency is held before the integrated life-safety test and before base-build handover, rather than spread thinly across activities.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead per zone/unit for the field — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
